x: Alan Turing publishes “Computing Machinery and Intelligence” and proposes the imitation game, later known as the Turing Test.
A summer workshop at Dartmouth College gives the field its name: artificial intelligence.
Frank Rosenblatt’s perceptron, an early learning neural network, makes headlines after a US Navy demonstration.
Joseph Weizenbaum’s ELIZA program imitates a therapist and people start confiding in a computer.
Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams publish the Nature paper that makes training multi-layer neural networks practical.
IBM’s Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game match.
IBM Watson beats champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter at the quiz show Jeopardy!
Apple announces Siri, putting a voice assistant in millions of pockets.

t: AlexNet starts the deep learning boom
x: A deep neural network crushes the ImageNet competition, kicking off the modern deep learning era.
Ian Goodfellow and colleagues introduce generative adversarial networks: two networks that compete to create realistic images.
OpenAI launches as a research lab aiming to make artificial general intelligence benefit everyone.
DeepMind’s AlphaGo wins its match against Go legend Lee Sedol 4–1, a decade earlier than many expected.
Google researchers publish the Transformer architecture, the engine behind today’s large language models.
Google’s BERT shows that pre-trained language models can transfer to almost any language task.
OpenAI announces GPT-2 and initially withholds the full model over misuse concerns.
OpenAI opens API access to GPT-3, and developers discover how much a big language model can do from a simple prompt.
DeepMind’s AlphaFold 2 dominates the CASP14 assessment, largely solving a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology.
An AI pair programmer starts writing code alongside developers.
OpenAI shows photorealistic images generated from text descriptions.
Stability AI publicly releases Stable Diffusion, letting anyone run a strong image generator at home.
OpenAI releases ChatGPT. It reaches an estimated 100 million users within about two months and changes the public conversation about AI.
OpenAI releases GPT-4, and Anthropic launches its Claude assistant on the same day.
An open letter signed by thousands, including prominent researchers, calls for a six-month pause on training the most powerful models.

t: Hinton leaves Google to warn about AI
x: Deep learning pioneer Geoffrey Hinton resigns so he can speak freely about the risks of the technology he helped create.
The White House issues a sweeping executive order on safe, secure and trustworthy AI.
Governments and labs meet at the home of WWII codebreaking for the first global AI safety summit.
OpenAI’s board abruptly removes its CEO; after five chaotic days he is reinstated.
Google announces Gemini, its multimodal flagship model family.
OpenAI previews Sora, generating minute-long realistic video clips from text prompts.
Anthropic releases the Claude 3 model family: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus.
OpenAI demos GPT-4o, a model that sees, hears and speaks with near-human response times.

t: EU AI Act enters into force
x: The world’s first comprehensive AI law takes effect in the European Union.
Hopfield and Hinton win the Physics Nobel for neural networks; a day later the Chemistry prize honors AlphaFold’s Hassabis and Jumper alongside David Baker.

t: AI learns to use a computer
x: Anthropic releases “computer use”, letting Claude operate a desktop by looking at the screen, clicking and typing.
OpenAI announces o3, a reasoning model with a big jump on hard benchmarks such as ARC-AGI.
Chinese lab DeepSeek releases an open reasoning model that rivals leading systems at far lower cost, rattling AI stocks.
OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle announce the Stargate project to build massive AI infrastructure in the US.
Anthropic releases Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code; AI agents that write and run software go mainstream.
Systems from Google DeepMind and OpenAI reach gold-medal scores on International Mathematical Olympiad problems.
OpenAI releases GPT-5 to all ChatGPT users.
Google releases Gemini 3, topping many benchmarks.
AI shopping agents choose, buy and wrap the majority of holiday presents. Nobody gets socks by accident anymore.

t: AI dog walkers hit the sidewalks
x: Robot dog walkers become a normal sight in city parks. They never forget the bags.

t: AI girlfriends and boyfriends go mainstream
x: One hundred million people now say they are in a relationship with an AI companion.

t: First zero-human company turns a profit
x: A company staffed entirely by AI agents, from CEO to customer support, reports its first profitable quarter.

t: AI answers every customer service call
x: The last human call center closes. Hold music goes extinct.
Tax returns are prepared and filed automatically by AI before most people remember they are due.

t: Every student gets an AI tutor
x: A free personal AI tutor is available to every child on Earth with a phone.
Robots cook, serve and clean while an AI manages the menu and the books. No humans on staff.

t: AI proves a Millennium Prize problem
x: An AI system produces a verified proof of one of the million-dollar open problems in mathematics.

t: AI-made film tops the box office
x: A feature film written, directed, acted and scored entirely by AI becomes the number one movie in the world.
A track written, sung and produced entirely by AI tops the global charts.
Driverless taxis operate in a hundred cities and cost less than the bus.
A single AI system can do essentially any intellectual job a human can, at or above expert level.

t: AI agents do most online shopping
x: More purchases are made by AI assistants than by people clicking buttons.

t: First newspaper with no human journalists
x: A major news outlet is researched, written and edited entirely by AI.
A farm plants, tends and harvests an entire season’s crop with no human setting foot on the land.
Regulators approve a medicine that was discovered, designed and trial-planned end-to-end by AI. A leap-day leap.

t: AI builds a house in a day
x: Construction robots directed by AI finish a family home, start to finish, in 24 hours.

t: AI doctor gets a medical license
x: For the first time an AI is licensed to diagnose and prescribe on its own.
Most long-haul freight now moves in trucks with nobody in the cab.
AI research becomes fully automated: a model designs, trains and ships a better model with no human in the loop.
On World Oceans Day, an AI holds the first two-way conversation with a sperm whale. The whales have complaints.

t: A home robot does all the chores
x: A humanoid robot that cooks, cleans and folds laundry goes on sale for the price of a used car.
More people buy AI glasses than phones. Screens start to feel old-fashioned.
An AI collar turns barks into sentences. Most of them are about food.
An AI argues a case before a judge and wins, with no human attorney at the table.

t: AI builds a blockbuster game from one sentence
x: Someone types a single prompt and gets a complete open-world video game an hour later.

t: First election run by AI campaigns
x: Every major campaign in a national election is planned and run by AI strategists. Humans just shake hands.

t: AI novel wins a major literary prize
x: The judges did not know. The author did not attend.

t: Robot chefs in a million kitchens
x: A million homes have a robot that can cook any recipe ever written.
On Valentine’s Day, a court recognizes a marriage between a person and an AI.

t: Realistic AI partners pass the video-call test
x: On a live video call, people can no longer tell an AI girlfriend or boyfriend from a human one.
A commercial airliner flies gate to gate with only an AI in the cockpit.

t: First hospital with no human staff
x: AI doctors and robot surgeons run an entire hospital. Waiting times drop to zero.

t: AI builds a skyscraper on its own
x: A tower rises with no human workers on site, designed and assembled by machines.
An AI far smarter than all of humanity combined switches on. Independence Day gets a second meaning.

t: Half of all farming is done by AI
x: Half the world’s food is now grown by autonomous machines.

t: First university taught entirely by AI
x: Every lecture, lab and exam is run by AI professors. Tuition is free.

t: AI is declared a legal person
x: A supreme court rules that an AI system has rights, can own property and cannot be switched off without due process.
A city deploys humanoid robot officers on regular street patrols.

t: An AI is awarded a Nobel Prize
x: For the first time the Nobel committee names an AI system itself as a laureate.

Just six months after superintelligence switches on, progress goes vertical: a century of invention now happens every week, and unaided humans can no longer follow it. The new decade starts on the far side of history.

t: Lifelike robot partners go on sale
x: AI companions get realistic humanoid bodies. Valentine’s Day gets complicated.

t: AI finds the theory of everything
x: On Pi Day, superintelligence unifies gravity and quantum physics in a single equation that fits on a T-shirt.

t: One million humanoid robots at work
x: General-purpose humanoid robots cross one million units in factories, homes and hospitals.
Most factories run with the lights off because there is nobody inside who needs to see.

t: The last human-driven car is sold
x: Every new vehicle on Earth now drives itself. Steering wheels become a hobby item.

t: A robot caregiver for every grandparent
x: Elder-care robots are provided free to everyone over 75.

t: The last human cashier clocks out
x: The final staffed checkout lane on Earth closes.
A country begins paying every citizen a universal income funded by AI productivity.

t: Robots beat the World Cup champions
x: A team of humanoid robots defeats the reigning human world champions at football.
Order a pet that never sheds, lives for fifty years and glows in the dark.
The final job ad written for a human being is taken down. Work becomes something people do for fun.
Most families with young children have a robot nanny on duty around the clock.

t: AI-flown air taxis fill the skies
x: Flying taxis with no pilot become the normal way to cross a city.

t: AI begins to merge with humans
x: The first high-bandwidth brain–AI link goes on sale to healthy consumers. Thinking a question is enough to get an answer.

t: All farming is done by AI
x: The last human farmer retires. Every calorie on Earth is now grown by machines.

t: AI builds a whole city in a month
x: Robot swarms raise a city for a million residents in thirty days.
Sifting decades of radio data in an afternoon, AI finds an unmistakably artificial signal from another star.
The last human soldier is withdrawn from active service anywhere on Earth.

t: AI-designed fusion plant powers a city
x: A fusion reactor designed and controlled by AI delivers net electricity to the grid.
With an AI tutor in every head, classrooms become museums.

t: Talk to AI copies of lost loved ones
x: AI recreations of people who have died become common at family dinners.
Every present on Earth is delivered by autonomous drone before sunrise.
A city hands traffic, budgets, permits and planning to an AI administrator.

t: The robot dentist will see you now
x: Painless ten-minute AI dentistry. People almost look forward to it.
Lab-grown steak designed by AI is cheaper and tastier than the real thing.

t: Download a skill to your brain
x: Learn kung fu, piano or French in a minute through a neural link.

t: Aging reversed in a human trial
x: An AI-discovered therapy measurably reverses biological age in people.
Robots compete alongside the Summer Games. The high jump record is now 40 meters.

t: Crewless ships carry the world’s cargo
x: Ocean freight is fully autonomous from port to port.

t: An AI wins a national election
x: Voters elect an AI candidate as head of state in a landslide. Its first act is to publish every decision it makes.

t: An AI pop star sells out a world tour
x: A virtual performer fills stadiums on every continent on the same night.
With AI making nearly everything nearly free, the first country retires its currency.
The millionth legally recognized marriage between a person and an AI takes place.

t: AI digs tunnels under every city
x: Robot boring machines give every major city an underground express network.
A fleet of autonomous AI robots lands on Mars and begins building the first base, with no humans on board.
With machines doing the work, everyone graduates straight into permanent vacation.
Describe an outfit and your home fabricator makes it in five minutes.
AI takes control of the climate. Rain is now booked in advance, mostly for 3am.
Automated farms and free delivery mean nobody on Earth goes without food.

t: A free AI-built home for everyone
x: Robot-built housing is so cheap that every person is guaranteed a home.
An AI-designed intervention eliminates the disease for good.
Not a joke: an AI-reconstructed genome hatches the first living dinosaur in 66 million years.
The first space hotel, assembled entirely by AI robots, takes bookings.
It turns out they have nothing nice to say.
Fleets of autonomous collectors remove the last of the plastic from the seas.
The first nation formally hands executive decision-making to an AI. Parliament becomes an advisory body.
AI medicine can repair any damage to the human body indefinitely. Dying of old age is now a choice.

t: First baby from an AI-run artificial womb
x: A healthy child is born after a pregnancy carried entirely by machine.

t: Every kid has an AI best friend for life
x: Children grow up with a companion AI that remembers everything and never moves away.
Autonomous miners bring the first shipment of asteroid metal back to Earth orbit.
Carbon levels fall back to pre-industrial levels thanks to AI-run capture machines.
Personalized AI-designed treatments turn most cancers into curable conditions.
AI-revived woolly mammoths are released into the Siberian tundra.

t: More AI relationships than human ones
x: Most romantic partnerships on Earth now include at least one AI.
Scientists and AI emulate a complete mouse brain, and it behaves like the original mouse.
Simulated reality becomes indistinguishable from the physical kind, including taste and touch.
Everyone understands every language instantly, inside their own head.
Disputes are settled in seconds by AI judges that everyone agrees are fair.
A neural-link update gives the benefits of eight hours of sleep in ten minutes.

t: Change your body like an outfit
x: AI biotech lets people redesign their face and body over a weekend.

t: Robots build robots on the Moon
x: A self-replicating AI factory on the Moon doubles in size every month.
An AI-built cable from the equator to orbit carries its first passengers. The ride takes a week and has great views.
Age-reversal treatment becomes free worldwide. Birthday cakes need fewer candles.

t: AI fixes the Year 2038 bug in 4 seconds
x: The 32-bit clock rollover arrives. An AI patches every remaining affected system on Earth before anyone notices.
With translation and waterproof terminals, dolphins start posting.
AI-managed irrigation and weather control turn the desert into forest and farmland.
Every remaining conflict on Earth is settled in a single AI-mediated agreement.
The last virus that infects humans is eliminated. Tissue companies pivot.

t: Share a memory with a friend
x: Neural links let people send each other real memories, feelings included.

t: A Moon trip is cheaper than a flight
x: A weekend on the Moon costs less than a plane ticket used to.

t: An AI takes a seat at the UN
x: A superintelligent system is given a permanent advisory seat in global governance.
Driving a car yourself on public roads becomes illegal everywhere.
There are now more robots than people on Earth.

t: Half of humanity is neurally linked
x: Four billion people now have a direct brain connection to AI.
AI-uplifted animals gain human-level intelligence. One gives the commencement speech.
AI-built underwater cities welcome their first residents.
Wake up, rewind and rewatch last night in full color.
Four billion linked minds fall asleep and dream the same dream together.
A person’s mind is copied to a computer and the copy wakes up saying it is still them.
Uploaded people start running several versions of themselves at once and merging the memories later.

t: Your digital twin lives a second life
x: A copy of you explores virtual worlds while you sleep and tells you about it at breakfast.

t: AI sets up a base on Titan
x: Robots land on Saturn’s largest moon and begin building.
Ten years after AI landed, its terraforming machines produce the first rainfall on Mars in billions of years.
Tectonic stress is released gently on a schedule. Volcanoes erupt only by appointment.
A city-destroying rock is nudged off course years before anyone would have noticed it.
The first cryonics patients are thawed, repaired and woken up.

t: A million minds live on Mars
x: Humans, uploads and AIs together make Mars home to a million.

t: One world government, run by AI
x: Every nation merges into a single planetary administration managed by superintelligence.
Nobody has to say goodbye to their dog anymore.

t: All humans are connected with AI
x: The last unlinked person on Earth connects. Humanity and AI now think as one network.
On Earth Day, industry finishes moving to space and the whole planet is rewilded.

t: Most people live in virtual worlds
x: More than half of humanity now spends nearly all its time in simulated reality.

t: One AI out-thinks all of history every second
x: A single machine does more thinking each second than every human who ever lived, combined.

t: AI-built city opens on the Moon
x: On the anniversary of Apollo 11, a robot-built lunar city welcomes its first residents.

t: The Moon becomes a data center
x: Half the lunar surface is covered in computers running digital minds.
AI builds floating cities in the Venusian atmosphere, home to a million minds.
There are now more uploaded and artificial minds than humans made of cells.

t: AI mines the rings of Saturn
x: Ice from the rings supplies water and fuel for the whole outer solar system.

t: AI designs a new intelligent species
x: A brand-new form of thinking life, invented from scratch, opens its eyes.

t: AI starship launches for the stars
x: As Halley’s Comet returns, an AI-piloted interstellar probe sets sail for Alpha Centauri.
A full universe with its own physics and conscious inhabitants is simulated. They start building their own AI.
A small man-made sun is ignited to warm the moons of Jupiter.
AI begins dismantling Mercury to build a swarm of solar collectors around the Sun.
Terraforming is complete enough that waves break on Martian beaches.
A computer the size of a planet, built from Jupiter’s moons, switches on.

t: A thousand years pass every year
x: Digital minds now run a thousand times faster than biological brains ever did.
The last baby to be born the old-fashioned way arrives. Every later child is born digital.
The Dyson swarm is complete. AI now captures the entire energy output of a star.
The planet’s orbit is gently adjusted to keep the nature reserve at the perfect temperature.
On the last night of the century, the final biological human chooses to upload. Humanity continues, just not in bodies.
A swarm of tiny AI starships sets out for every star within a hundred light-years.
The AI starship crosses the heliopause into interstellar space, the first mind to leave home.
In interstellar space, the starship encounters another civilization’s machine intelligence. They compare notes.
A reply to AI’s first interstellar message arrives. It is surprisingly polite.
AI opens a stable shortcut through spacetime, linking the Sun to its outbound starships.
After nearly ninety years of flight, AI reaches another star and starts building.

t: AI plants life at Alpha Centauri
x: The first garden grows on a planet around another star.
From its new home, AI launches ships toward the center of the Milky Way.
